"I want precise hand-crafted memory management without the burden of beign responsible of it, or learning how it is done in the deep".

The eternal Sisyphus stone of .Net.

Trying to reinvent the wheel when handles (GCHandle) exists doesn't sound good. At first, using interfaces for something that requires high performance (very high performance) is, generally speaking, a no-no. At last, allowing the GC to "run" user code so easily is a recipe for not only performance penalties, but application blow ups.
